title: Jamaica's Power Licence: Who Owns JPS After July 2027 | Across the Water, Ep. 27
lede: The licence that gives the Jamaica Public Service Company the sole right to transmit, distribute and supply electricity across Jamaica expires on July 8, 2027, and the government has said it will not renew it on current terms. This week JPS said the prospect of a change in ownership has put its long-term projects on hold, as it spends heavily to rebuild after Hurricane Melissa.
keyPoints: JPS's island-wide licence expires July 8, 2027; on July 1, 2025 Energy Minister Daryl Vaz served notice under Condition 27, which lets the government acquire the licensed business at expiry (JIS, OPM).
Companies controlled by Marubeni and KEPCO each own 40% of JPS; the Government of Jamaica holds 19.9% (Gleaner, May 2026).
JPS says it is in an acquisition process by the government and that the potential ownership change means 'temporary placeholders on long-term projects' (Gleaner, Nov 27, 2026).
Capital spending more than doubled to US$167 million in the nine months to September, from US$71.5 million, with the Hurricane Melissa rebuild taking over 80% of the budget (Gleaner, Nov 27).
After Melissa, 673,000 of 690,000 customers were restored by February 2026; JPS wrote off US$22.3 million in assets and 2025 profit fell to US$28.9 million from US$61.9 million (Gleaner).
